clips.text_zh: 又係呢條友問BTC定黃金好。睇完都係嗰句，揀錯邊就食10年灰。我揀BTC，但黃金真係穩陣。真係好揀，我一早唔使咁灰。10年後再睇啦。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, which would you choose? What makes your choice better than the other one? This same debate hits /biz/ every few months, and the answer usually depends on whether you trust central banks more than code.

signal.rationale: OP is a vibe-check question with no entry, no target, no stop — pure debate thread

clips.text_en_b2: The Bitcoin versus gold debate resurfaces on /biz/ every couple of months, and people keep asking which asset you should hold for the next decade. Honestly, the whole thing boils down to whether you place more faith in central banks or in code, because the crowd backing each side rarely changes its mind. I've gone with BTC myself, although gold genuinely remains the safer bet, and ten years from now we'll see who called it right.
clips.text_en_c1: The perennial Bitcoin-versus-gold debate resurfaces on /biz/ with monotonous regularity, and whichever camp one backs, a decade of regret awaits those who choose poorly. Personally, I have committed to Bitcoin, though I concede that gold retains a fundamentally defensive character that crypto still struggles to match. Were the decision genuinely straightforward, I would not have spent the better part of ten years second-guessing myself. The crux of the matter ultimately hinges on whether one places greater trust in algorithmic scarcity or in the centuries-old conviction of central banks. We shall reconvene in 2034 and render judgement accordingly. 🙏
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial Bitcoin-versus-gold question resurfaces on /biz/ with metronomic regularity, each iteration ostensibly seeking definitive resolution while in practice confirming that conviction is merely a proxy for temperament. The original poster frames the dilemma as a ten-year binary: monetary sovereignty encoded in immutable software, or millennia of accumulated trust in a tangible, if unproductive, asset. Replies inevitably bifurcate along ideological lines, with those distrustful of central-bank discretion gravitating toward BTC and the more risk-averse anchoring themselves to bullion's established track record. What renders the debate ultimately irresolvable is the asymmetry of failure modes; gold disappoints gradually, whereas Bitcoin's volatility curve can vaporise portfolios overnight. The thread thus becomes less an investment inquiry than a referendum on institutional faith.

clips.text_zh: DOGE三日內上太空，要買嘅就快。爆咗都仲會升，未爆就放，唔好做SNL 2.0。我又心痕想All-in，但又驚食多餐學費。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Doge goes to space in 3 days and you're not buying. If this thing blows up it will still move up first, so why not ape a bit, then sell before it becomes SNL 2.0? Or maybe it will just start the hype cycle again. A clean pump-and-dump setup if the launch is real.

signal.rationale: OP implies buy-the-launch, sell-before-SNL setup; short window tied to a catalyst in 3 days

clips.text_en_b2: Doge is supposedly heading to space within three days, and if that launch actually goes ahead it could easily set off another hype cycle. The smart play, as plenty of traders are pointing out, is to throw a bit in and cash out before it turns into the SNL 2.0 disaster everyone remembers. Even if the thing dumps afterwards, momentum tends to carry the price up first. Personally, I'm tempted to go all in, although another round of tuition fees would sting.
clips.text_en_c1: Doge is purportedly launching into orbit within seventy-two hours, and anyone still on the sidelines deserves to remain there. Should the announcement prove legitimate, the token will almost certainly spike on sentiment before any sell-the-news event unfolds, which is precisely why a measured position—entered early and exited before the inevitable SNL-style collapse—remains the rational play. The setup is textbook pump-and-dump territory, albeit one dressed up in the trappings of genuine aerospace ambition. I find myself once again tempted to overcommit, though the tuition I have paid in prior cycles counsels against it. 🧐
clips.text_en_c2: Doge's imminent suborbital jaunt has galvanised the speculative community into a state of anticipatory euphoria, with seasoned pump-watchers parsing launch telemetry as though it were scripture. The prevailing thesis, articulated with characteristic /biz/ bravado, posits that even a catastrophic mission failure would generate sufficient short-term liquidity to permit a measured entry followed by disciplined exit prior to the SNL-induced reckoning that decimated holders last cycle. Sceptics counter that previous catalysts of comparable magnitude produced asymmetric drawdowns precisely because retail enthusiasm peaked prematurely. The underlying calculus resembles a classic momentum trade dressed in memetic clothing: capital is deployed not on fundamentals, which are negligible, but on the reflexive behaviour of an audience conditioned to treat spectacle as alpha.

clips.text_zh: 今日去地盤做斜坡condition survey，soil nailing位見到地下水滲出。要寫入GI report，factor of safety要check返Tommy話ok先交。返屋企再睇FE。考牌都未完，屌。
clips.text_en_b1: How do you know when to bulk enough to cut and escape skinnyfat? The poster says he cut from 83kg down to 65kg, then lean-bulked back to 80kg while flat benching 3x8 at 60kg, squatting 90kg and deadlifting 120kg. The numbers are close to mine now, so this hits home.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ bulk vs cut thread; learner maps it to site cycles
clips.text_en_b2: How do you figure out when you've cut enough weight to escape skinnyfat territory? The original poster explains that he dropped from 83kg down to 65kg, then lean-bulked back up to 80kg while flat benching 3x8 at 60kg, squatting 90kg and deadlifting 120kg. Those figures line up closely with where I'm at, so it really hits home. Civil engineers in Hong Kong run through a remarkably similar cycle: trim the project down, rebuild it, then verify the load.
clips.text_en_c1: I spent the morning on a slope condition survey at an active site, where groundwater seepage was clearly visible along the soil-nailing interface. The findings must be incorporated into the Ground Investigation report, and the revised factor of safety calculations cannot be submitted until Tommy signs off on the methodology. I shall review the finite element output again this evening, provided I can stay awake past the absurdity of the licensing exam timeline. The cyclical nature of this profession—cut, rebuild, verify—mirrors the recomp transformation that the original poster describes with admirable precision.
clips.text_en_c2: A reconnaissance inspection of an existing slope revealed persistent groundwater seepage adjacent to the soil-nailing array, a finding that necessitates formal documentation within the forthcoming Ground Investigation report. The structural ramifications are non-trivial, since elevated pore-water pressures materially erode the factor of safety against translational failure, particularly during the monsoon recharge cycle. Pursuant to site protocol, the assessment must be corroborated by Tommy before submission, lest the residual risk profile prove unacceptable to the reviewing party. This deferral, while procedurally sound, underscores the broader pedagogical challenge confronting candidates still navigating the Fundamentals of Engineering examination, where theoretical competence must be reconciled with field pragmatism and the unrelenting logistics of professional licensure.

clips.text_zh: 睇緊reinforced concrete嘅load path由slab落到beam落到column再落foundation。鋼嗰邊一樣，moment connection點解用，點check welding。FE真係多嘢背。
clips.text_en_b1: Weighted calisthenics are the best workout you can do. It will give you an aesthetic physique, the bodily control becomes off the charts compared to a bodybuilder or a powerlifter, and you become strong without getting fat. Being able to do a planche or handstand push-up is more impressive than a 2-plate bench. No one cares how much you bench press.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ calisthenics thread mapped to load-path thinking
clips.text_en_b2: Weighted calisthenics arguably offers the most well-rounded workout you can commit to, since it builds an aesthetic physique while keeping bodyweight control completely off the charts. Unlike bodybuilders or powerlifters, you come out strong without piling on unnecessary mass, and pulling off a planche or handstand push-up is far more impressive than grinding out a two-plate bench. The principle mirrors load path logic perfectly: strength flows through the cleanest route, never the bulkiest one.
clips.text_en_c1: I have been tracing the load path through a reinforced concrete frame: from slab to beam, beam to column, and column down to the foundation interface. The steel alternative requires comparable rigour, particularly with respect to moment connections, where weld quality and base-plate detailing govern the entire transfer mechanism. The Fundamentals of Engineering examination demands that one internalise all of this procedural detail, which is precisely why my evenings have been swallowed by formula sheets and AISC provisions. Were the discipline straightforward, the qualification would hardly command the professional weight that it does.
clips.text_en_c2: The elegant mechanics of load path tracing in reinforced concrete, whereby gravitational forces cascade sequentially through slab, beam, column, and ultimately foundation, offers an instructive parallel to calisthenic training philosophy. In structural steelwork, analogous continuity is achieved through moment connections whose adequacy hinges upon weld inspection protocols and rigorous quality assurance. Both disciplines demand that practitioners internalise load trajectory intuitively, rather than relying on rote computation, since failure modes invariably originate at points of discontinuity. The volume of material mandated for the FE examination reflects this integrative burden: candidates must synthesise disparate analytical frameworks into a coherent mental model, lest superficial familiarity precipitate the kind of catastrophic oversight that no retrospective correction can remedy.

clips.text_zh: AI bubble爆咗都唔代表GPU會平，因為全部畀人熔咗回收。真係黐線。又係學費。仲驚過FE考試，怕自己份工畀AI搶埋。
clips.text_en_b1: You thought you could get cheap GPUs after the AI bubble pops? Think again — they're all getting melted down. If the AI hype dies, the supply of cheap second-hand GPUs won't appear because the chips are being physically destroyed and recycled. Civil engineers feel the same squeeze: when AI touches site reporting, the cheap tools dry up first.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on GPUs being melted, no cheap supply
clips.text_en_b2: Anyone assuming cheap GPUs will flood the second-hand market once the AI bubble finally bursts is in for a nasty surprise, because the chips are being physically melted down and recycled. Even if the hype collapses tomorrow, that steady supply of affordable hardware simply won't materialise, and the whole situation feels absolutely unhinged. As civil engineers we feel the same squeeze when automation creeps into site reporting, since the cheaper tools always dry up first.
clips.text_en_c1: Anyone expecting a flood of affordable GPUs once the AI bubble finally deflates is in for a profound disappointment, because the hardware in question is being physically dismantled and recycled rather than offloaded onto secondary markets. The chips, quite literally, are being melted down into raw silicon, which eliminates the usual post-crash arbitrage that bargain hunters tend to anticipate. For those of us in adjacent technical fields, the anxiety runs deeper than mere hardware costs: if AI encroaches upon site reporting and design automation, the most accessible tools will inevitably vanish first. We have all paid enough tuition.
clips.text_en_c2: The sanguine expectation that an AI-sector contraction would precipitate a glut of affordable second-hand GPUs constitutes a fundamental misreading of contemporary semiconductor economics. Datacentre operators, cognisant that depreciated accelerators retain residual value principally through resale channels, have increasingly resorted to physical destruction and subsequent precious-metal recovery, thereby sterilising the secondary market entirely. This supply-side attrition insulates incumbent pricing from the deflationary pressures that historical technology cycles typically generate. For practitioners whose professional futures are entwined with infrastructure adjacent to AI deployment, the implications extend well beyond hardware acquisition costs; when generative models encroach upon functions previously requiring human judgement, the inexpensive tools that supported those workflows evaporate first.

clips.text_zh: 有 /pol/ 仔話關稅收咗21 trillion。唔知真定假，但個post下面全部係笑柄。香港呢邊傾緊AI泡沫，兩邊一樣膠。
clips.text_en_b1: We took in 21 trillion from tariffs? The OP just posts a tweet and asks the question — no source, no chart, just a giant number thrown at the board. The replies are pure shitposting about printing money and trade deficits. Same energy as a GI report with no borehole data attached.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ tariff 21T tweet, replies are pure shitpost
clips.text_en_b2: Some /pol/ user is claiming tariffs brought in a staggering twenty-one trillion, and frankly nobody knows whether the figure is genuine or pulled out of thin air. The original post offers nothing but a single tweet, no source, no chart, just a colossal number lobbed at the board, and the replies have descended into pure shitposting about printing money and trade deficits. Across the pond in Hong Kong, threads are debating the AI bubble instead, although both conversations feel equally clueless at this point.
clips.text_en_c1: A /pol/ regular is now circulating claims that recent tariff collections have generated some twenty-one trillion in revenue, though the original post offers neither source data nor a coherent methodology to substantiate the figure. The replies, predictably, have devolved into facile shitposting about money-printing and trade imbalances, with no participant pausing to interrogate the underlying arithmetic. The intellectual texture here is indistinguishable from that of a geotechnical interpretive report published without the corresponding borehole logs, and the parallel underscores how both online discourse and professional practice suffer when foundational evidence is treated as optional.
clips.text_en_c2: A thread positing tariff revenues of twenty-one trillion dollars has descended, predictably, into the sort of unfalsifiable claim that anonymous forums reward with derision rather than scrutiny. The original post, devoid of source material, methodological framework, or temporal specification, functions less as economic analysis than as provocation, inviting respondents to compete in absurdist elaboration. Replies dutifully oblige, with citations of money-printing, trade-deficit arithmetic, and the obligatory references to intercontinental ballistic trajectories. The spectacle mirrors the professional frustration of receiving a Ground Investigation submission absent the requisite borehole logs, which is to say the evidentiary scaffolding without which any conclusion remains merely performative.

clips.text_zh: 日本自閉症協會話Mii-chan同Miss Yamada 2027年動畫版有問題，話將弱勢社群當娛樂。Kodansha回應緊。睇完標題我諗起Demon Slayer，呢啲嘢年年都嘈。
clips.text_en_b1: Japan Autism Association raises concerns over Mii-chan and Miss Yamada. The group says the anime turns vulnerable people into entertainment. Kodansha and its production committee announced on July 26 that the anime is due in 2027. The manga follows a young woman who struggles to read social cues and is inferred to be mentally disabled.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread on Mii-chan autism portrayal ethics
clips.text_en_b2: The Japan Autism Association has publicly raised concerns over the upcoming Mii-chan and Miss Yamada anime, arguing that the adaptation effectively turns a vulnerable community into entertainment. Kodansha and its production committee responded that the series is still scheduled for 2027, having announced the date back on July 26. The manga itself follows a young woman who struggles with reading social cues and is widely inferred to be mentally disabled. These controversies crop up every year, not unlike the annual Demon Slayer debates.
clips.text_en_c1: The Japan Autism Association has formally raised concerns regarding the forthcoming anime adaptation of Mii-chan and Miss Yamada, scheduled for release in 2027, on the grounds that the source material risks commodifying neurodivergent individuals for mass entertainment. Kodansha and its production committee acknowledged the criticism on July 26 and are reportedly preparing a measured response, though the controversy itself echoes a recurring pattern that recurs annually whenever sensitive subject matter crosses from niche manga into mainstream adaptation. The discourse around Demon Slayer and similar properties demonstrates that such objections are hardly unprecedented within the industry's recent memory.
clips.text_en_c2: The Japan Autism Association has formally objected to the forthcoming 2027 anime adaptation of Mii-chan and Miss Yamada, contending that its narrative apparatus reduces neurodivergent individuals to objects of consumable amusement rather than subjects of authentic representation. Kodansha, alongside its production committee, announced the project on the twenty-sixth of July, prompting immediate backlash from advocacy organisations who perceive the source material as insufficiently interrogative of its own premise. The manga's protagonist, a young woman evidently struggling with social cognition, occupies narrative terrain that critics argue demands more circumspect handling than popular serialisation typically permits. Comparable controversies have periodically attended adaptations such as Demon Slayer, suggesting that the tension between commercial viability and representational responsibility remains an industry-wide structural problem rather than an isolated editorial miscalculation.
